About the Position

The CVISS Lab (Computer Vision for Smart Structure Laboratory) and iNDT Laboratory at the University of Waterloo, Canada, are recruiting graduate researchers and postdocs for condition and safety assessment of infrastructure using non-destructive testing (NDT) combined with computer vision and AI.

Labs & Supervisors

  • CVISS Lab (Dr. Chul Min Yeum): computer vision / deep learning for infrastructure inspection, UAV/drone-based inspection, image-based structural assessment.
  • iNDT Laboratory (Dr. Giovanni Cascante): non-destructive testing and material characterization using ultrasonic/wave-based methods, GPR, geophysical and sensing techniques.

Research Focus

AI-enhanced NDT for structural health monitoring (SHM) of reinforced concrete and steel structures. Resilience of the built environment.

Requirements

Required:

  • Undergraduate, MSc or PhD in Civil, Mechanical, Electrical Engineering or related field (undergrad to direct-entry PhD route exists).
  • Signal/image processing expertise, including AI/ML libraries.
  • Experience with NDT methods: visual inspection, ultrasonic waves, electromagnetic waves.
  • Programming: Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW or similar.
  • Proficient spoken/written English.

Preferred:

  • Hands-on NDT sensors/equipment: ultrasonic transducers, laser vibrometers, fiber-optic sensors, GPR, infrared sensors, EM-wave antennas.
  • Numerical simulation of solid mechanics/elastic waves (COMSOL, Abaqus, ANSYS).
  • Knowledge of construction materials and structural behavior.
  • Publication record in NDT or SHM.

Duties

  • Coordinate research projects and timelines.
  • Plan and run lab and field NDT experiments.
  • Prepare specimens, sensor setups, and calibration.
  • Develop algorithms/software for data analysis, visualization, defect detection, and condition assessment.
  • Write reports, peer-reviewed papers, proposals, budgets, and progress reports.
  • Support workshops, demos, lab visits, and knowledge transfer.

Application Process

  1. Email detailed CV to cmyeum@uwaterloo.ca with subject line "Position Application".
  2. Review lab work at https://cviss.net/ beforehand.
  3. Shortlisted candidates invited to interview. No reply means not progressed.
  4. If matched, submit formal application to Waterloo Graduate Studies.

Funding

Paid research positions funded through research assistantships, often combined with teaching assistantships and awards. Typical doctoral packages CAD 20,000-30,000+/year; postdoc salaries CAD 45,000-65,000/year. Exact amount confirmed in offer.

Start Dates

Winter 2027 (January) or Spring 2027 (May).

Official Link

  • CVISS Lab: https://cviss.net/
  • Waterloo CEE: https://uwaterloo.ca/civil-environmental-engineering
  • Waterloo Graduate Studies: https://uwaterloo.ca/graduate-studies

Important Notes

  • Rolling review until positions filled.
  • International applicants require Canadian study permit (grad students) or work permit (postdocs).
  • Never pay any processing or visa fee to anyone claiming to represent the lab.

Contact

  • Email: cmyeum@uwaterloo.ca

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be sent to the contacts above or raised through the channel given on the official announcement page.

About University of Waterloo

University of Waterloo is a public research university in Ontario, Canada. It offers undergraduate, graduate and doctoral programmes across engineering, mathematics, science, business-related fields, arts and health. Its cooperative education model connects study with work experience, while research groups investigate topics ranging from digital technologies to infrastructure and environmental challenges.

Official website: https://uwaterloo.ca

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: Rolling Review - No Fixed Deadline. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
